zero_prep_card.objective: Children retell the story and say that Jesus has authority over the storm.
zero_prep_card.opening: Ask children to make quiet rain sounds with their fingers, then louder storm sounds, then stop together.
say: The disciples were in a real storm and were frightened.
Jesus spoke, and the wind and sea obeyed Him.
The disciples asked, "Who is this?" The miracle showed His authority.
We can tell Jesus when we are afraid, and we can ask trusted people for help.
ask: What can we do when we feel afraid?
zero_prep_card.do: Use the room to make a storm-to-calm soundscape, then place four story events in order.
zero_prep_card.close: Pray: Jesus, thank You that You are powerful and present. Help us tell You and trusted people when we are afraid.
materials: Four event cards or four blank sheets of paper

activities.title: Storm to Calm Sequence
materials: Four event cards: crossing, storm, Jesus speaks, calm
steps: Let children place them in story order.
Act out each scene using sounds and movements.
Repeat the big idea together after the calm.
activities.learning_link: Reinforces narrative order, cause and effect, and Jesus' authority.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Assign four children one event each and have the class stand them in the correct order.

closing.prayer_prompt: Thank Jesus for His authority and ask for help to speak honestly when afraid.
closing.take_home_line: Jesus has authority over creation, and I can bring my fear to Him.

essential.label: Short
essential.use_case: Minimum viable lesson for a teacher with little preparation time or a shortened class.

outline.label: Connect
outline.instructions: Create quiet rain sounds, build to a storm, then stop together.

outline.label: Read and retell
outline.instructions: Read Mark 4:35-41 in short sections and retell the concrete sequence.

outline.label: Understand
outline.instructions: Notice what changed when Jesus spoke and what this shows about Him.

outline.label: Do
outline.instructions: Complete the Storm to Calm Sequence activity.

outline.label: Respond
outline.instructions: Name one safe response to fear, repeat the take-home line, and pray.

standard.label: Standard
standard.use_case: Default Sunday session with reading, discussion, activity, and response.

outline.label: Connect
outline.instructions: Make storm sounds and discuss what a storm can feel like.

outline.label: Read
outline.instructions: Read Mark 4:35-41 with brief pauses for observation.

outline.label: Observe
outline.instructions: List what the disciples did, what Jesus did, and what the wind and sea did.

outline.label: Discuss identity
outline.instructions: Explore why the disciples asked who Jesus is and avoid promising a trouble-free life.

outline.label: Activity
outline.instructions: Order and act out the story events.

outline.label: Close
outline.instructions: Review the big idea, use one quiz item orally, and pray.

extended.label: Extended
extended.use_case: Longer session with additional textual work, activity, comparison, or assessment.

outline.label: Connect
outline.instructions: Build a storm soundscape and establish classroom safety for discussing fear.

outline.label: Dramatic reading
outline.instructions: Read or retell the passage with assigned sound and movement roles.

outline.label: Text observation
outline.instructions: Separate details stated in Mark from details the group imagined.

outline.label: Who is Jesus?
outline.instructions: Discuss the disciples question and, for older children, note the canonical echo of God stilling storms without forcing technical terminology.

outline.label: Sequence activity
outline.instructions: Complete, explain, and repeat the story sequence.

outline.label: Review
outline.instructions: Use the quiz and correct the false promise that Christians never face frightening situations.

outline.label: Respond
outline.instructions: Practise naming prayer and trusted-adult support as safe responses to fear, then pray.

discussion_questions.question: What did the disciples see, hear, and feel?
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Separate details stated by the text from imagined details.

discussion_questions.question: What happened immediately after Jesus spoke?
Why do you think the disciples asked, "Who is this?"
discussion_questions.foundation_prompt: Because even the wind and water obeyed Him.
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Connect authority over creation to Jesus' identity without requiring technical vocabulary.

discussion_questions.question: What is one safe thing you can do when afraid?
discussion_questions.foundation_prompt: Pray or tell a trusted adult.

preparation.passage_context: Mark has just recorded Jesus teaching in parables. The crossing and miracle turn attention from what Jesus teaches to who He is.
text_observations: The danger and fear are not imaginary; water was entering the boat.
Jesus is asleep, the disciples wake Him, and He directly addresses both the storm and their fear.
The narrative ends with the disciples' question about Jesus' identity rather than with a general lesson about weather.
interpretation_notes: The strongest theological point is Christological: creation responds to Jesus' command.
Psalm 107 provides a canonical echo in which God stills storms, but avoid presenting this as a direct quotation or proof-text inside the children's lesson.
theological_guardrails: Do not promise that Jesus will stop every storm, illness, conflict, or frightening event immediately.
Do not shame children for fear. The lesson calls for trust and honest dependence, not emotional denial.
Do not turn every detail in the boat into a symbol.

likely_questions.question: Why was Jesus sleeping?
likely_questions.purpose: Acknowledge His real human tiredness without overexplaining.
likely_questions.foundation_prompt: Jesus had been teaching and was tired.
likely_questions.extension_prompt: Mark shows Jesus genuinely human and yet exercising authority over creation.

likely_questions.question: Will Jesus stop every bad thing?
likely_questions.foundation_prompt: Jesus is with us and we can ask for help.
likely_questions.extension_prompt: This passage shows His authority; it does not promise immediate removal of every hardship.

interactive.title: Storm and Stillness
interactive.instructions: Use hands and voices to act out the storm, then freeze in silence when Jesus speaks.

family.parent_note: Avoid asking a child to disclose a private fear in front of others. General examples are sufficient.
family.prayer: Jesus, You are powerful. Help us trust You and ask for help when we are afraid.
questions: What does the storm obeying Jesus show us about Him?
Who can you talk to when you feel afraid?

flow.instructions: Make quiet rain sounds, then loud storm sounds, then stop.
Read Mark 4:35-41. Let the child make a motion for each main event.
Ask what changed when Jesus spoke and what the disciples wondered about Him.
Put four events in order: crossing, storm, Jesus speaks, calm.
Each person names one safe way to respond to fear, then pray.

family.weekly_action: When someone in the family feels afraid, pause, listen without teasing, and pray together.
family.parent_intro: This activity helps children see what the story says about Jesus. It does not promise that every frightening situation disappears immediately.
family.title: From Storm to Calm

editorial.scripture_text_policy: Store references and editorial paraphrases in the prototype. Add licensed translation text only after permissions and attribution rules are confirmed.
editor_notes: This is a vertical-slice draft designed to test schema, rendering, timing, and workflow rather than a final published lesson.
Teacher and Family experiences must render from this same canonical object.
Teacher timing is tested through Essential (25 minutes), Standard (40 minutes), and Extended (55 minutes) delivery profiles.

do_not_ask: Do not require children to disclose traumatic events or private fears to the group.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Validate fear, offer prayer, and remind children they may speak privately to a trusted adult.
safeguarding.escalation_note: Follow normal safeguarding policy if a child voluntarily discloses harm or immediate danger.

accessibility.reading_level: Adult reads Scripture; child-facing instructions use short concrete sentences.
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Prefer wind, waves, afraid, command, and calm over abstract theological vocabulary.
neurodiversity_supports: Show the sequence visually before acting it out.
Allow a child to watch rather than make loud sounds.
sensory_notes: Storm sounds may be uncomfortable; offer a quiet role and keep volume controlled.
non_reader_support: Use pictures or gestures for each event.
Accept pointing or acting instead of verbal answers.

learning.foundation_objective: Retell the main action in Mark 4:35-41 and state that Jesus has authority over the wind and sea.
learning.extension_objective: Explain why the disciples asked who Jesus was and name one faithful response when afraid.
know: Jesus commanded the storm and it became calm.
understand: The miracle points to Jesus being more than an ordinary teacher.
Fear can be spoken honestly rather than hidden.
practise: Name a fear in safe, general language and pray for help.
become: A child who increasingly trusts Jesus and responds to others fear with care rather than ridicule.
success_evidence: The child orders four story events correctly.
The child says that Jesus had authority over the storm.
The child names prayer or asking a trusted adult for help as a faithful response to fear.

quiz.question: Where were Jesus and the disciples?
What did Jesus command?
quiz.explanation: The storm became calm after Jesus spoke.

quiz.question: True or false: The story promises that Christians will never face frightening situations.
quiz.explanation: The story shows Jesus' authority and presence, not a promise of a trouble-free life.

quiz.question: Put the events in order.
quiz.explanation: This is the narrative sequence in Mark 4.

puzzle.title: What Happened Next?
puzzle.instructions: Arrange the story cards from first to last.

core.big_idea: Jesus has authority over creation and is present with frightened disciples.

claims.statement: A severe storm arose while Jesus and the disciples crossed the lake.
Jesus spoke to the wind and sea, and the storm became calm.
The event reveals that Jesus has authority over creation.
Followers may bring fear to Jesus, but the passage does not promise that every frightening situation will end immediately.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not promise children that faith always removes danger or difficult feelings at once.

core.interpretation_skill: Retell sequence, identify cause and effect, and connect the action to Jesus without forced symbolism.
core.metanarrative_position: Jesus' ministry: the promised King reveals authority over creation.
